---
title: "Episode 9: The Pitch Deck"
subtitle: "Programming with Python · Tutorial 09"
---

The pitch meeting is Friday, and the investor gave one instruction: **"Bring me
charts I can't argue with."** Last week you turned the data room into numbers
she could trust; this week those numbers have to be *seen*. Same file,
`orders_messy.csv`, now with pictures: you pick the chart that fits each
question, save it as a picture file, and end the lab with a deck of six. Tobi has
already "built the deck": two slides and one argument for a new rider. Your
job is to **supervise**: catch the chart she can argue with before she does.

## Run the lab on your laptop

The lab is a Python script again. It runs in the `python-labs` folder, next to
last week's files.

1. Download the script and move it into your `python-labs` folder.
   `orders_messy.csv` is still there from last week; if not, download it again:

   [Lab script](../labs/lab_09_pitch.py){.btn .btn-primary download="lab_09_pitch.py"}
   [Orders data](../labs/orders_messy.csv){.btn .btn-primary download="orders_messy.csv"}

2. In Zed, open the `python-labs` folder, then the terminal (`` Ctrl+` ``).
3. Run `uv run python lab_09_pitch.py`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## No Zed on your laptop, or only an iPad?

Use a **GitHub codespace**: a Linux computer that runs in a browser tab.

1. Sign in at [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces) and open
   last week's codespace again. If you have none, start the **Blank** template
   and follow the [uv guide](../general/uv.qmd) (the macOS or Linux lines) in
   its terminal, down to `uv add pandas matplotlib`.
2. Go into the folder with `cd python-labs` and download the script. The
   second line is only needed in a new codespace:

   ```bash
   curl -O https://python.tobiasvlcek.com/labs/lab_09_pitch.py
   curl -O https://python.tobiasvlcek.com/labs/orders_messy.csv
   ```

3. Run `uv run python lab_09_pitch.py`.

To look at a chart, click its PNG file in the file list on the left. A
codespace has no Zed, so keep the chatbot open in a second tab for AI help.
:::

The first run stops with `AssertionError: Task 1: not attempted yet.`, as it
did last week: the script checks every task and stops at the first one you
have not solved yet. The very first run can take a little longer, because
matplotlib sets up its fonts once.

A script has no cell that could show a chart, so every chart goes into a
picture file in `python-labs`. Task 2 in the script shows the three lines
that end every chart. To look at a picture, click its file in Zed's project
panel, the file list on the left.

::: {.callout-important}
## Look at your charts

The checks only test the form of a chart: that it has a title, that its bars
add up to your own numbers. They cannot see whether the chart tells the truth.
And **two things in Tobi's deck are wrong without any task saying so**: one is
in his numbers, one is in what he claims. No check catches either of them.
:::

When every check passes, the script puts your six charts side by side into
`pitch_deck.png` and prints a block that starts with `SHOW THIS IN CLASS`.
Show both to your lecturer.

Checkpoint 5 next week is still handed in from the browser, and the script
labs no longer practise that. So take two minutes before you go: open today's
last exercise, [ex_09_e](https://python.tobiasvlcek.com/notebooks/ex_09_e/),
press **Cmd/Ctrl+S**, then menu → Download → **Download Python code**, and find
the file in your Downloads folder.
